title: Why Korean elevators have no 4 👻 사 = 4 #learnkorean
caption:
In Korean, 4 is 사 (sa) — and 사 (死) also means death. Same sound.
So many buildings in Korea label the 4th floor F, for Four.

Count with me:
일 (il) 1
이 (i) 2
삼 (sam) 3
사 (sa) 4

Not every building does this, but you'll see it a lot.

SYNK LAB
#learnkorean #studykorean #koreanlanguage #koreanculture
pinnedComment: Is there an unlucky number in your language? 👇
alt: A needle-felted coral ghost mascot in a tiny brass elevator searches for floor 4: the buttons read 1, 2, 3, F, 5. A Korean voice counts 일, 이, 삼, 사; at 사 the music stops, the lights flicker and a tiny white ghost peeks out beside the glowing F button. On screen: 4 = 사, death = 사. An F patch stitched over the 4 lifts at one corner. The doors open on a dim hallway where small white ghosts at a tea table all turn to stare; one lifts a teacup. The mascot slams the doors shut and sighs with relief — and then a tiny ghost appears on its head and whispers 사.
